stories.title: Reform proposes £30 tax rebate for HMRC phone delays
stories.summary: Reform UK economy spokesman Robert Jenrick announced that under a Reform government, taxpayers kept on hold by HMRC for more than 30 minutes would receive a £30 credit off their tax bill. The policy also proposes tying senior HMRC officials' pay to customer service performance targets.

stories.title: New counter-terror hub launched to protect British communities
stories.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood secured Five Eyes agreement at the Five Country Ministerial in Sydney to establish a permanent joint Countering Violent Extremism Hub in London. The hub will pool intelligence, expertise, and resources across Five Eyes partners to improve coordination against violent extremism.

stories.title: Forty children reported missing from UK asylum hotels still not found
stories.summary: A Guardian investigation reveals that forty children who were reported missing from UK asylum hotels in 2023 have still not been located. The Home Office faces continued scrutiny over the welfare and tracking of unaccompanied minors in asylum accommodation.

stories.title: British couple in Iran prison able to make call — 'enormous relief'
stories.summary: The family of Craig and Lindsay Foreman, a British couple detained in Tehran's Evin Prison on espionage charges they deny, reported they were able to speak with them — described as an 'enormous relief'. The FCDO has faced pressure to arrange consular visits and medical checks for the couple.

stories.title: Professor David Strain appointed as DWP Chief Medical Advisor
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions has appointed Professor David Strain as its new Chief Medical Advisor. The role is key to advising on welfare, health assessments, and disability benefits policy.

stories.title: Gloucestershire records first deadly bluetongue virus case
stories.summary: Gloucestershire has recorded its first case of bluetongue virus, a potentially deadly insect-borne disease affecting livestock, according to DEFRA data. Twelve new BTV-3 cases were confirmed across England on 25 August, with new outbreaks in Dorset and North Yorkshire highlighting the spread of the disease.

stories.title: Wes Streeting describes 'unbelievable volume' of homophobic abuse as defence secretary
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, the UK's first openly gay defence secretary, has spoken publicly about receiving a massive volume of homophobic abuse online since taking up the role. Streeting said the experience highlighted lingering prejudice, while also noting strong support from within the Ministry of Defence.

stories.title: Nvidia sales soar on rapid buildout of AI data centres
stories.summary: Nvidia reported surging sales driven by rapid investment in AI data centre infrastructure — a key trend shaping UK AI and technology policy as BIST oversees the government's science and innovation agenda. The AI data centre boom has raised questions about energy consumption and the need for UK regulatory frameworks.

stories.title: NHS Cyber Security Operations Centre issues 87 alerts in 2026 so far
stories.summary: An NHS CIO update for August 2026 reveals the NHS Cyber Security Operations Centre has issued 87 cyber alerts this year, including 20 classified as high priority. NHS digital and cyber teams continue to respond to an elevated threat environment across the health service.

stories.title: Psychiatrists say NHS is failing child sexual abuse victims in adulthood
stories.summary: Psychiatrists have raised concerns that the NHS is failing adult survivors of childhood sexual abuse, citing inadequate mental health provision. The NHS Alliance highlighted this as a key area requiring urgent attention in health and care sector developments.

stories.title: CWU members vote 96.8% to reject Royal Mail's Optimised Delivery Model
stories.summary: Communications Workers Union (CWU) members turned out at 75% and voted 96.8% to reject Royal Mail's proposed Optimised Delivery Model (ODM), a major industrial relations development that could affect service delivery and staffing across the network.
